intro: In contracts and meetings, accept and except, or won't and want, change the meaning completely. Say them clearly and check when you are not sure.
Use headphones. Listen first, then choose.

parts.title: 1. Which word do you hear?

The works have been delayed by four working days.

data.end: Well done! Clear pronunciation means fewer mistakes on site. Practise the phrases again before your next meeting.

data.h: A call from the employer's head office
data.scene: Conference call · the line is not very clear
intro: On real projects you hear many accents. Mr Rajesh Iyer manages the employer's assets from Mumbai, and he calls about the handover file.

lines.t: Good afternoon Jasur, this is Rajesh Iyer from the employer's head office in Mumbai. I'm calling about the handover file for Block B.
Good afternoon, Mr Iyer. The file was handed over on the thirtieth of June: the manuals, the as-built drawings, the certificates and the warranties.
Very good. Our asset team also needs a digital copy. Could you upload everything to the project portal by Friday?
Yes, the scanned file is ready. I'll upload it by Friday morning and send you the link.
Excellent. One more thing: who do we contact if a defect appears during the liability period?
The helpdesk address on page two of the manual. We respond within five working days, and faster for anything urgent.

qs.q: What does Mr Iyer ask for?
opts: A digital copy of the handover file on the portal

qs.q: By when will Jasur upload it?
Where is the defect contact address?
opts: On page two of the manual

qs.q: How fast does the contractor respond to defect reports?

data.end: Great! Accents and phone lines are part of real projects. If you are not sure, confirm: Just to confirm, by Friday morning?

data.h: Role-play practice with an AI partner
intro: Want more speaking practice? An AI chat assistant can play the other person. Choose a role-play, copy the prompt and practise for 10 minutes.

cards.title: Variation negotiation
cards.goal: Your director wants a glass partition in the lobby one week before handover. Negotiate with me: the process, the price (around three thousand dollars) and the effect on the handover date.
cards.prompt:
Let's do an English role-play for construction. You are Mr James Porter, the client's representative. I am a site engineer on a project in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
Situation: Your director wants a glass partition in the lobby one week before handover. Negotiate with me: the process, the price (around three thousand dollars) and the effect on the handover date.
Rules: speak at B1–B2 level, one short turn at a time, and wait for my reply. Push back a little, so I have to explain, ask questions and confirm details. Focus on: variations, would cost, written instructions and polite firmness.
After 8–10 turns, stop and give me feedback: 3 things I did well, 3 corrections (my sentence → a better sentence) and 5 useful phrases for this situation.

cards.title: A payment question
cards.goal: Ask me about payment application number eight: what was applied, certified and paid, why twenty thousand dollars was not certified, and when the money is due.
cards.prompt:
Let's do an English role-play for construction. You are Ms Anna Weber, the lender's monitoring engineer. I am a site engineer on a project in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
Situation: Ask me about payment application number eight: what was applied, certified and paid, why twenty thousand dollars was not certified, and when the money is due.
Rules: speak at B1–B2 level, one short turn at a time, and wait for my reply. Push back a little, so I have to explain, ask questions and confirm details. Focus on: the payment cycle, passive forms and exact figures.
After 8–10 turns, stop and give me feedback: 3 things I did well, 3 corrections (my sentence → a better sentence) and 5 useful phrases for this situation.

cards.title: The handover walk
cards.goal: We walk the building one day before handover. Ask me what is still outstanding, what happens if something breaks in October, and what changes when the taking-over certificate is issued.
cards.prompt:
Let's do an English role-play for construction. You are Mr Tom Reed, the client's building manager. I am a site engineer on a project in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
Situation: We walk the building one day before handover. Ask me what is still outstanding, what happens if something breaks in October, and what changes when the taking-over certificate is issued.
Rules: speak at B1–B2 level, one short turn at a time, and wait for my reply. Push back a little, so I have to explain, ask questions and confirm details. Focus on: handover documents, the defects liability period and reassuring a client.
After 8–10 turns, stop and give me feedback: 3 things I did well, 3 corrections (my sentence → a better sentence) and 5 useful phrases for this situation.

tips: Copy the prompt and paste it into Claude or ChatGPT. Use voice mode if you can – speaking is better than typing.
If you don't understand, say: “Sorry, could you repeat that more slowly?”
Do not paste real company documents, prices or personal data.
